key_insight: The paper combines large language models with fuzzy logic and formal rules to make disease diagnosis more explainable and verifiable.
clinical_relevance: It could help clinicians review AI-generated diagnoses with transparent reasoning paths that can be checked against clinical guidelines.
method: LLMs extract medical entities, temporal relations, and fuzzy symptom patterns from patient narratives and guidelines.
The extracted information is translated into a symbolic knowledge base using fuzzy logic and declarative rules.
A two-stage pipeline performs diagnostic pattern induction and then verifies diagnoses with a logic programming engine.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on public benchmarks and reported performance comparable to state-of-the-art LLMs, while also producing interpretable and formally verifiable reasoning chains.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will still depend on accurate entity extraction and careful rule maintenance, since errors in the symbolic translation could affect the final diagnosis.
paper_title: Uncertainty Reasoning with Large Language Models for Explainable Disease Diagnosis
